definition: Misrepresent means to describe something in a false or misleading way.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word misrepresent. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know misrepresent should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The trailer misrepresented the film so thoroughly that audiences arrived expecting a comedy and sat through two hours of grief.
Slant is milder than misrepresent — a slanted account tilts the emphasis while keeping the picture recognizably true.
Falsify goes further than misrepresent: to misrepresent is to arrange a false impression, while to falsify is to change the underlying facts themselves.

To mislead is to aim at the audience's belief by any means — words, images, or well-chosen silence. Grammar tells the two verbs apart: you mislead a person, while you misrepresent the thing being described. Misleading needs no description at all; misrepresenting is deception built out of one.

To distort is to twist a true picture out of shape — stretching one part, shrinking another — the way a funhouse mirror handles a face. Misrepresent is the broader accusation: a description can misrepresent through outright lies, half-truths, or careful omission, with no twisting needed.

Misrepresent means to describe something in a false or misleading way.
The pamphlet misrepresented the internship: 'newsroom experience' turned out to mean fetching coffee two floors below the newsroom, and the 'stipend' was a bus pass.
Misrepresent covers every flavor of false description — outright lies, half-truths, and truths arranged to deceive.
Slanting merely tilts the emphasis, and falsifying changes the facts themselves; misrepresenting aims at the picture in the audience's head.
Misrepresent is the careful accusation: it says a description was false or misleading without claiming every word was a lie — which is why lawyers and fact-checkers lean on it.
Fabricate, in this unit, builds falsehood outright; misrepresent can work entirely with truths, arranged to deceive.

The series' most famous sequence shows a lone wolf bringing down an elk in deep snow — proof, the narrator says, of the solitary hunter's power.
Field notes released this spring tell it differently.
Three wolves ran that elk; the film crew cut the other two out of the frame, and the 'wild' kill was followed within minutes by a veterinary check, off camera.
Biologists say the edit misrepresents the animal outright: wolves are cooperative hunters, and calling one animal's share of a pack's work a solo feat rewrites the species.
The producers have promised a corrected cut; the original, meanwhile, has been streamed forty million times.
